description: Symptom → cause → action decision tree for Guitar Rig. Deltas are normalised 0–1 and represent ONE step, not a final value: apply, listen, repeat.
symptoms.clipping.ear_test: Roll the guitar volume back halfway. If the harshness disappears instantly, it is clipping, not tone.
symptoms.clipping.causes.0.cause: interface input gain set too high
symptoms.clipping.causes.0.user_action: Play the hardest chord you actually use; the input meter should peak between −12 and −6 dBFS, never in the red.
symptoms.clipping.causes.4.actions.0.not: acts ahead of every gain stage in the chain; fixes the cause, not the symptom
symptoms.clipping.safety_net.0.note: a level ceiling; it is a safety net, not a fix
symptoms.clipping.pitfalls: Lowering PV does not help if the clip already happens at the interface input.
Lowering preamp V1 reduces the clip AND the distortion. To drop level only, use master V2.
symptoms.low_volume.causes.2.actions.1.n: check the pedal is not rolled down
symptoms.low_volume.pitfalls: Do not raise preamp V1 to gain volume: that adds distortion. Use the master.
symptoms.hiss.ear_test: Halve V1/Gn. If the hiss drops with it, the chain is amplifying noise: treat the cause.
symptoms.hiss.causes.0.cause: excessive drive or preamp gain (root cause)
symptoms.hiss.causes.1.cause: no noise reduction in the chain
symptoms.hiss.causes.1.actions.0.repeat_: hiss gone while you are not playing
symptoms.hiss.causes.1.actions.5.note: Range attenuates instead of muting: avoids the slamming-door effect
symptoms.hiss.pitfalls: Too high a threshold eats sustain — see “Notes cutting out”.
A gate does not remove hiss while you play, only in the gaps.
symptoms.hum.measurement.condition: narrow peaks at the mains frequency
symptoms.hum.ear_test: Turn your body while holding the guitar. If the level changes, it is electromagnetic pickup. Touch the strings: if it stops, it is grounding.
symptoms.hum.causes.0.user_action: Change position, move away from monitors, power supplies and chargers, check the grounding.
symptoms.hum.pitfalls: A gate is the wrong tool for hum: it destroys sustain and the hum returns under the note.

symptoms.fizz.distinguish_from.hiss: fizz only appears while you play; hiss is constant and a gate removes it

symptoms.fizz.causes.0.cause: missing cabinet, or the wrong one
symptoms.fizz.causes.0.actions.1.note: move off the cone centre; the most effective control here
symptoms.fizz.causes.1.cause: too much high frequency from the distortion
symptoms.fizz.causes.1.actions.2.note: a low-pass drops everything above; better than a bell cut for fizz
symptoms.fizz.pitfalls: Lowering amp Treble also kills the useful attack at 3–4 kHz. Work on the cabinet and mic instead.
symptoms.notes_cutting.measurement.condi: abrupt drop instead of a smooth decay
symptoms.notes_cutting.pitfalls: If you need a high threshold to hold back the hiss, the real problem is excess gain — see “Hiss”.
symptoms.muffled.causes.0.actions.0.note: mic toward the cone centre; the most powerful control and the least obvious
symptoms.muffled.causes.1.cause: not enough presence or treble from the amp
symptoms.muffled.pitfalls: If mud at 250–500 Hz is masking the top, adding treble makes it bright AND muddy. Check “Muddy” first.

symptoms.harsh.distinguish_from.fizz: harshness bites on the attack, around 3–5 kHz; fizz is continuous noise above 6 kHz

symptoms.muddy.causes.0.actions.0.note: the single most transformative cut on electric guitar
symptoms.muddy.causes.0.actions.6.note: set mi/ma to cover the 100–1000 Hz range
symptoms.muddy.causes.0.actions.8.note: a high-pass clears the sub that only eats headroom
symptoms.muddy.pitfalls: Mud at 250–500 Hz gets mistaken for “too much bass”. Cutting at 80 Hz does not fix it and leaves the sound thin.
symptoms.thin.pitfalls: Body lives at 100–250 Hz; mud at 250–500 Hz. If it got heavy AND woolly, you aimed at the wrong band.
symptoms.lost_in_mix.context: Only meaningful while listening to the full mix, never to the guitar soloed.
symptoms.lost_in_mix.causes.0.cause: the guitar's own band is empty
symptoms.lost_in_mix.pitfalls: A scooped tone sounds impressive soloed and is the worst possible choice in a mix. Keep a separate preset for each situation.
symptoms.weak_palm_mute.causes.0.cause: uncontrolled low end smearing the attack
symptoms.weak_palm_mute.causes.0.actions: low drive with high level: cuts bass before the distortion, the classic Tube Screamer trick
symptoms.not_enough_gain.causes.0.action: fuzz is a different category, not “more distortion”
symptoms.not_enough_gain.pitfalls: Amps that are clean by design (Twang Reverb, AC Box, Tweedman, Jazz Amp, Tweed Delight) do not become high gain no matter the setting. Change amp.
The high-gain ones: Gratifier, Van 51, Rammfire, Sledgehammer, MeZone.
symptoms.mushy.causes.1.cause: too much bass hitting the distortion
symptoms.mushy.causes.1.actions.0.note: the number one cause of mush
symptoms.squashed.causes.1.cause: high gain acting as a compressor
symptoms.washed_out.pitfalls: Reverb is the biggest single reason a guitar vanishes in a mix. Use less than feels right when playing alone.
symptoms.muddy_reverb.causes.0.cause: too much low end in the tail
check mic by mic, pi1 through pi8
presets using CrossOver split by frequency; the high half may be inverted
symptoms.too_wide.causes.0.actions.4.not: this component exists only for width; check it first
outside_guitar_rig.0.cause: buffer too large, or the wrong driver
outside_guitar_rig.1.cause: buffer too small for the CPU
outside_guitar_rig.2.where: the gain knob on the interface
outside_guitar_rig.3.symptom: hum that changes as you move
outside_guitar_rig.4.cause: old strings or a rolled-off tone control
outside_guitar_rig.5.cause: bad cable or a noisy pickup
common_amp_params.V1|Gn: input / preamp gain — how much distortion
common_amp_params.V2|Mast: output / master volume — level without changing distortion
common_amp_params.Pr|Prs|p: Presence — acts in the power stage, sounds different from treble
common_amp_params.Rsp: Response — how fast the amp reacts
common_amp_params.Var: Variac — supply voltage; tightens the sound
amp_exceptions.Plex: V1 = Bright Volume, V2 = Warm Volume — two channels summed, not gain + master
amp_exceptions.Van 51: R0 = Rhythm Pre Gain, L1 = Lead Pre Gain, P5 = Post Gain, H14 = HiGainInput
amp_exceptions.AC Box: Vol = Normal Volume, Br = Brilliant Volume — two channels
amp_exceptions.High White: nv = Normal Vol, bv = Brilliant Vol, Mst = Master
amp_exceptions.Tweedman: VB = Volume Bright, VN = Volume Normal
amp_exceptions.Tweed Delight: vb = Volume Bright, vn = Volume Normal; only t = Tone, no B/M/T
amp_exceptions.Gratifier: Gn = Gain, Mast = Master; M is Mode, not Mid
amp_exceptions.Rammfire: Gn = Gain, Mast = Master; M is Mode, not Mid
amp_exceptions.Ultrasonic: g = Gain, v = Volume, Mst = Master
amp_exceptions.Hot Solo+: P0 = Normal, P1 = Overdrive, M6 = Master, O2 selects the channel
amp_exceptions.Sledgehammer: g = Gain, v = Volume; c = Contour with f = Frequency form a sweepable mid
amp_exceptions.MeZone: D = Distortion, V = Volume; the only one with PRE-distortion EQ (PB, PQ, PM, PT)
amp_exceptions.Jazz Amp: V = Volume; clean by design, em = Ensemble Mode
amp_exceptions.Bass Pro: G = Gain, D = Drive, V = Volume; graphic EQ with bands labelled in Hz
amp_exceptions.TransAmp: D = Drive, V = Volume; A selects the amp, CM enables cab & mic
ui.title: Symptom reference — Guitar Rig
ui.order_rationale: Do not skip stages. Each one contaminates the next: adjusting EQ while the signal clips is pointless, because the harshness that bothers you is the clip, not the tone. Setting a gate before fixing excess gain masks the noise and eats sustain. Setting reverb before tone makes you compensate EQ with space, and the result sits distant and unfocused.
ui.family_hint_level: is it clipping? is there headroom?
ui.band_desc_sub: guitar does not live here; it only eats headroom
ui.band_desc_body: warmth. Missing = no body. Excess = covers the bass
ui.band_desc_definition: note attack. Missing = **lost in the mix**
ui.band_desc_air: under distortion this is mostly rubbish. A real speaker rolls off above ~5–6 kHz
ui.sym_fizz: Fizz — harsh hiss inside the distortion
ui.sym_notes_cutting: Notes cutting out, chopping, dying early
ui.sym_muddy: Muddy, woolly, no definition in the low end
ui.sym_lost_in_mix: Lost in the mix (with a band)
ui.sym_weak_palm_mute: Palm mutes with no punch, floppy low string
ui.sym_muddy_reverb: Reverb or delay muddying the low end
ui.sym_mono_collapse: Disappears or goes hollow in mono
ui.verify_present: Confirm these exist in the chain
ui.amp_exceptions: Exceptions — on these amps V1/V2 do not mean gain and master
ui.footer: Deltas are **one step**, not a final value. Apply, listen, repeat. Frequencies in Hz are targets; the matching parameter is normalised 0–1 and the exact mapping was not decoded — set it on screen. Components named here may not exist in the preset you are using.
